task: Make the File Datasource 10-file upload limit configurable via env var (default 10) and add concurrent batch processing for file uploads to support hundreds of files without performance degradation.

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: Config (FILE_DATASOURCE_MAX_UPLOAD_COUNT env var), IndexKnowledgeBaseFileRequest validator, UpdateKnowledgeBaseFileRequest validator, FileDatasourceService (process_files_batch + upload_and_prepare_files), AzureFileRepository (thread-safety), GCPFileRepository (thread-safety), FileSystemRepository (thread-safety)

requirements_clarity.label: S
requirements_clarity.gaps: Original plan anticipated a YAML config change; implementation simplified to a single env var in Config — a pragmatic narrowing that was resolved without ambiguity.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Concurrent file uploads via ThreadPoolExecutor introduce race conditions in container/bucket creation across three storage backends; correct error handling required for mid-batch failures and rollback
technical_risk.mitigation: ThreadPoolExecutor capped at max_workers=min(3, len(files)); ResourceExistsError/Conflict caught on container creation in AzureFileRepository and GCPFileRepository; rollback logic added in _write_extracted_files_with_rollback

key_reasoning.reason: Four distinct components required coordination: (1) Config — one env var added; (2) two API request model validators updated to reference the config value; (3) FileDatasourceService — new process_files_batch() using ThreadPoolExecutor and upload_and_prepare_files() helper; (4) three repository implementations (Azure, GCP, filesystem) required thread-safety fixes to handle concurrent container/bucket creation from the new batch worker threads.

Base M (3) — ThreadPoolExecutor concurrency is a standard stdlib pattern. Bumped to L (4) by the 'Performance/Scalability as primary concern' red flag: the ticket explicitly required batch processing to support hundreds of files without degradation, and the implementation introduced concurrent I/O with race-condition handling and mid-batch rollback logic across three storage backends.

14 implementation files changed (excluding 5 planning docs): 7 source files modified, 3 test files modified, and 4 new test files created covering the three repository classes and request model validators. 10 distinct directories spanned.

Four layers touched: API layer (request model validators + router handler), Service layer (FileDatasourceService batch logic), Repository layer (thread-safety in all three storage backends), and Config/Infra layer (new env var). No DB schema migration; no external service calls added.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M (3) to L (4): 'Performance/Scalability as primary concern' — batch processing required to prevent performance degradation when uploading hundreds of files is an explicit primary requirement.
